title: Blackhole Tracker: BHSM Boundary Interpretation of Compact-Lens Mass, Motion, and Conditional Response

authors.name: Norman P. Carberry
authors.provenance: Established author facts reused under the user's current instruction 'Thats it, the same as always'; contact and identity recovered by coordinating agent from preserved manuscripts.

abstract: Blackhole Tracker provides reproducible compact-lens inference with explicit Berger–Hopf Standard Model (BHSM) interpretation: one effective exterior is counted once. A local app, command line, Python package and notebooks support resolved pairs and native unresolved photometry. A frozen pilot processes 100 OGLE-III events and 76,344 measurements: 89 fail its adequacy screen, eleven are not rejected and two pass stricter archival follow-up criteria. A versioned atlas reconciles this pilot with 59 published parallax events, retaining 155 distinct source/event directions, literature revisions and all failed assessments. Three qualified or disputed investigation targets remain distinct from black-hole identifications. Mass, lens position, distance and absolute motion remain unresolved; duration is not mass. A 2022 benchmark rejects rectilinear photometry-only fits. A separate joint benchmark uses 12,521 photometric measurements and 21 two-coordinate HST positions; three frozen noise candidates fail residual-structure checks. Reviewed corrections remove numerical-reference dependence, admit physical nuisance profiles and preserve unavailable motion uncertainties. The optional scalar–tensor calculation bounds boundary states in its retained exterior, but two projected modes vanish and the leading apparent-mass response is degenerate with shear. The product supports auditable screening, localization and conditional response tests. No new black-hole interpretation, measured BHSM core dynamics, detectable envelope or horizon classification is established.
